title: Feature Scaling — Meters Beside Millimeters
key_insight: Feature scaling changes the numeric rulers without changing which row is which. Standardization centers a feature and measures it in typical-spread units.
body:
## Meters Beside Millimeters

One column measures height near 2 meters and another records salary near 100,000. A distance calculation mostly notices salary because its numbers are larger.

Feature scaling changes the numeric rulers without changing which row is which. Standardization centers a feature and measures it in typical-spread units.

Fit the ruler on training rows, then reuse it for test and production rows. Letting test values set the ruler leaks information.
common_mistakes: Fitting the scaler before the train/test split.
Using min-max scaling without checking extreme outliers.
Centering a huge sparse matrix until it becomes dense.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “Meters Beside Millimeters” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Distance methods and gradient-based models can be distorted or slowed by mismatched feature units.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Meters Beside Millimeters” story, explain Feature Scaling without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
